objective: Prospectively preserve synchronized public Binance Spot and USD-M execution evidence needed to replace historical proxy slippage and capacity inputs without inventing history.

prospectiveWindow.lateStartLaw: A late start does not move the interval; missed time is explicit missing coverage.
prospectiveWindow.protocolChangeLaw: Any material protocol, universe, threshold, fee-scenario, or estimator change creates a new campaign and a new future interval.

normalization.quantityLaw: Greatest common legal base quantity whose exact walked Spot entry cost is at most the requested quote budget.

spot.sequenceLaw: Buffer first; refetch while snapshot lastUpdateId is below first U; discard u<=lastUpdateId; first retained U<=lastUpdateId<=u; thereafter ignore stale u<local and resync when U>local+1.

usdM.sequenceLaw: Buffer first; discard u<lastUpdateId; first retained U<=lastUpdateId<=u; thereafter require pu==previous u and resnapshot on mismatch.
usdM.productDiscriminator: st=1 when present; st=2 is rejected

receiveAndContinuity.generationLaw: Each open, reconnect, forced 24-hour rotation, gap, or overflow increments generation and requires a fresh snapshot bridge; stale generations cannot mutate or restore eligibility.
receiveAndContinuity.dropLaw: Any unrecorded drop, sequence gap, clock discontinuity, or queue overflow makes every intersecting evaluation window ineligible.

pointInTimeConfiguration.bindingLaw: Store canonical response bytes, retrieval clocks, status, headers needed for rate-limit provenance, and SHA-256; a changed digest starts a new configuration epoch.
pointInTimeConfiguration.uncertainChangeLaw: The interval between the last old digest and first new digest is configuration-uncertain and ineligible.
pointInTimeConfiguration.filterLaw: Evaluate exact decimal PRICE_FILTER, LOT_SIZE, MARKET_LOT_SIZE, MIN_NOTIONAL, NOTIONAL and applicable percent/reference filters; unknown, duplicate, malformed, account-state, or unmodeled filters block legal-size proof.
pointInTimeConfiguration.precisionLaw: Never substitute pricePrecision for tickSize or quantityPrecision for stepSize.
pointInTimeConfiguration.marketReferenceLaw: Sizing, slippage, and filter reference prices are distinct and never substituted.

rpi.mergeLaw: Never merge or subtract standard and RPI books unless a future protocol proves common sequence identity and executable eligibility.
rpi.capacityLaw: Standard coherent depth may establish a displayed executable lower bound; missing standard depth, snapshot-edge exhaustion, or any reliance on RPI returns UNKNOWN or NOT_PROVEN, never zero.
rpi.tradeLaw: Preserve USD-M aggregate q and nq independently; q-nq is bucket-level RPI-involved quantity evidence, not fill eligibility.

feesFundingAndSlippage.feeLaw: Apply each explicit scenario rate to each exact walked leg notional; unknown rates remain null and block net results.
feesFundingAndSlippage.displayedBookSlippage: Exact depth-walk cashflow relative to that leg's contemporaneous touch, reported diagnostically and not double-counted.
feesFundingAndSlippage.latencyStressLaw: Additive adverse sensitivity on every one of four fill legs after displayed-book walking; it is not an observed fill.
feesFundingAndSlippage.fundingLaw: A streamed rate is prospective only. Settled cost uses complete funding-history rows, actual funding timestamps, mark prices, rateType, and witnessed position intervals. For the short USD-M leg, positive funding is a credit and therefore a negative cost.
feesFundingAndSlippage.missingFundingLaw: Zero only when complete interval evidence proves no funding boundary; otherwise UNKNOWN.

capacity.definition: Greatest common legal base quantity observable on both coherent standard ladders while each walked leg and the pair remain within the declared impact ceiling.
capacity.snapshotBoundaryLaw: Reaching the captured depth edge prevents a total-capacity claim.

journal.chain: Each record binds the preceding record SHA-256, protocol SHA-256, configuration SHA-256, session, generation, ordinals, clocks, source identity, payload and record hash.
journal.seal: Acceptance requires an externally supplied exact record count and terminal record SHA-256; a valid prefix is not a complete journal.
journal.segmentLaw: Segments are immutable after seal; segment and corpus manifests are published last and exclusively, with exact byte length, line count, file SHA-256, first and last record hash, previous manifest hash, and completeness counters.
journal.tamperResponse: Never repair in place; preserve corrupt bytes, classify, and start a new recovery-linked segment.

replay.determinismLaw: Identical admitted evidence and parameter bytes produce byte-identical receipts across path, timezone, locale, and PYTHONHASHSEED.
replay.failureLaw: Admission validates external seal, canonical bytes, record chain, ordinals, lifecycle, generations, protocol/config bindings, segment inventory and completeness before emitting any derived cost/capacity input.

reporting.eligibility: Only complete entry and exit synchronized cuts with complete point-in-time public configuration, exact fee scenario, and complete intervening funding evidence.
reporting.multipleTestingLaw: Subsets are descriptive and cannot establish a positive family result without the accepted S-META1 familywise procedure; small-N subsets are marked INSUFFICIENT below 20 complete trips.
reporting.campaignCoverageGate: Report prospective result eligible only if every pair has at least 20 complete trips and at least 90 percent of scheduled trip slots are complete; otherwise mechanics/evidence remain usable but profitability is UNKNOWN.
reporting.positiveClaimLaw: This substrate does not itself produce VERIFIED_POSITIVE, build/no-build, M0, or capital decisions.

publicArchiveBoundary.checksumLaw: Any later archive input must bind official URL, sidecar bytes, ZIP bytes, byte length, retrieval time, schema, timestamp unit and SHA-256; replacement objects create a new revision.

mechanicsSmoke.purpose: Prove parsing, clocks, append/seal, tamper rejection and deterministic replay mechanics only.
